correctness.rationale: The quadric e1=e2 is smooth via independent gradients, and five F2 rational points prove it nonsplit. At all five, e3 has vanishing differential on the quadric. On its F4 Segre splitting, each Frobenius graph has bidegree (2,1) or (1,2), hence meets the (3,3) cubic with expected length nine unless contained; five double intersections force at least ten, proving both components, and bidegree exhaustion gives exact reduced scheme. The graphs meet transversely at precisely P1(F4), proving five ordinary nodes and full component geometry. Projective-line counts supply N_n for every n and then the zeta rational function. Exact independent enumeration via included C++ verifies n=1..6; finite enumeration is not used to prove the universal formula.

value.rationale: The prime-two degeneration of a canonical genus-four highly symmetric curve is a natural motivated arithmetic-geometric boundary of the standard equations. The exact geometric decomposition into Frobenius-exchanged twisted cubics, five nonsplit nodes and all-extension zeta function provide a complete model-specific description, not a trivial numerical slice or routine consequence of only knowing its arithmetic genus.
